a:r.a:t: About one minute. Point at the gold token, then trace the lines back.

Attention is how a transformer uses context. When the model produces a new token, here 'mat', it looks back at every earlier token and weighs how relevant each one is. That's how 'it' can refer to something three sentences back.

To do that, each earlier token contributes a key and a value at every layer. Recomputing those for the whole conversation on every new token would be wasteful, so inference engines store them. That store is the KV cache.

The cache is stored data, not another neural network. It grows by a fixed amount with every token, which is why long context costs memory. In a few slides we'll calculate exactly how much for Qwen3-8B.
